saw_lines: Watch buyers pick a piece that says something about them, then wear it for years and rarely replace it.
So the sale is won in the first line, where the buyer decides if this watch is for them.
Your 10 of 30 ads run one exact copy, so buyers see the same story twice. Give each of those 10 ads a new opening line and a dial close up.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 21 Oct 2026
points: The same copy runs in 10 of 30 ads, so a man who sees one twice learns nothing new. Keep the copy, but give each of the 10 ads a new opening line and a dial close up.

None of your 30 ads shows a proof number, so a buyer weighing a watch like this has nothing concrete to trust. Pick one real number, such as a review count or orders shipped, and lead the ads with it.

10 of 30 ads open on “built for action”, and the rest are single use, so you have no second hook to compare. Test two new openers against it: one on the skeleton movement, one on the Freedom Chrono colour.
0 of 30 ads mention an offer, so a first time buyer sees no reason to act today. Put a first order offer or a bundle in line one of the 10 Skeleton Chrono ads, the ones that run most.

ads_1: Skeleton movement close ups with two new openers replacing the built for action line
